gen and gen~ can now take a typed-in @expr attribute to set an expression; this is basically anything you can type into a codebox. The @expr attribute can only be typed into the gen and gen~ object boxes. It will not appear in the object action menu or the object reference page. The mc.gen variation runs several gen instances in parallel; you can use the new mc_channel and mc_channelcount operators to create channel-specific expressions, however note that the only way to use multiple channels is with the @chans attribute; mc.gen cannot auto-adapt as other mc objects can (because it's not really a signal object!)

You may enable @autoexport to export code whenever the genpatcher is edited. However, in order for this to work properly, the following must be true: 

1) audio must be on
2) a previous manual export must have occurred
3) a valid value for the exportfolder attribute must be set
specify the folder to export code to
export whenever the genpatcher is edited

The code from any gen~ object can be exported to C++ simply by sending the 'exportcode' message. If the @exportfolder attribute has not been set, it will prompt for a folder to save the file too. Subsequently all code will be exported to this folder.

Code export is subject to change in future updates.
fraction of available CPU time used
Gen~ has a built-in capability to measure how much of the available CPU time is being utilized by the hosted genpatcher.

In addition to the standard Gen operators, the gen~ domain supports additional operators specific to the audio domain.
Many of the Gen operators are common to gen~, jit.gen, jit.pix, and jit.gl.pix objects For the full list of operators and constants see the Gen Common Operators reference vignette.
The gen~ supports reading and writing persistent memory using the data and buffer storage objects.
